Maintainable software architecture has several key characteristics:

## Clear Separation of Concerns
- Each component has a single, well-defined responsibility
- Business logic is separated from infrastructure concerns
- User interface is decoupled from data processing

## Loose Coupling
- Components depend on interfaces/abstractions rather than concrete implementations
- Changes in one module don't cascade through the entire system
- Dependencies flow in one direction when possible

## High Cohesion
- Related functionality is grouped together
- Components have focused, coherent purposes
- Internal elements work together toward a common goal

## Consistent Patterns and Conventions
- Standardized naming conventions and coding styles
- Consistent error handling approaches
- Predictable project structure and organization

## Comprehensive Documentation
- Architecture decisions are recorded with rationale
- API documentation stays current
- System diagrams and component relationships are documented

## Testability
- Components can be tested in isolation
- Clear boundaries enable unit and integration testing
- Test coverage provides confidence for changes

## Modularity
- System is broken into manageable, replaceable pieces
- Well-defined interfaces between modules
- Ability to modify or replace components independently

## Observability
- Logging, monitoring, and debugging capabilities are built-in
- System behavior is visible and traceable
- Performance bottlenecks can be identified

The goal is creating a system where developers can understand, modify, and extend the codebase efficiently without introducing bugs or breaking existing functionality.
